summary.text: 介 is used for “between” and related meanings such as “mediate.” Early forms are described as a human figure flanked by marks, but the marks’ meaning and the graph’s original construction remain disputed.

formation.text: Early forms are described as a person with two or four flanking marks, a picture-based construction whose details remain disputed. The received 說文 analysis divides the graph into 八 and 人, but that later account does not prove the original construction.

components.text: Early-form descriptions identify a human figure corresponding to 人. In this proposed picture-based analysis, it depicts a person; whether it was a distinct component in the original graph remains uncertain. The received 說文 analysis later identifies 人 as one part.

Early forms are described with flanking dots, but their identity and role are disputed: they have been interpreted as marks for “between,” armor or covering, secondary status, or ritual sparks. Identifying them as modern 丶 is tentative.

history.text: Early forms are described as a person flanked by two or four marks; the reports do not establish a sequence among these forms.
In clerical script, the following component was regularized as 人. The side form 亻 is also recorded as a variant. This later graphic history does not settle the character’s earliest construction.

uncertainties.text: The flanking marks’ identity and meaning, and the graph’s original construction, remain disputed. Proposed interpretations include “between,” armor or covering, secondary status, and a ritual-intermediary account.
Reported oracle-bone meanings and a bamboo-slip use have not been checked against the underlying inscriptions or slip edition, so their individual readings and dates remain unresolved.
The supplied glosses include shell or scale, armor, assistance, and intermediary, but do not establish when these arose or whether they developed from one another.

A reported use of 介 for 個 may reflect reuse of the written sign for another word. The proposed mechanism is sound resemblance, but its direction, date, and historical sound basis remain unresolved: the cited Mandarin readings are jiè and gè, and the Baxter–Sagart reconstructions differ as well.

senses.period: early textual examples reported; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: Reported early textual examples use 介 for being situated between two states. This is the earliest meaning supported here, not proof of the graph’s original meaning.

senses.period: oracle-bone use reported; individual inscription dates and readings unverified
senses.text: Oracle-bone uses are reported with the meanings “junior” or “secondary,” but their readings remain disputed and the underlying inscriptions have not been verified.

senses.gloss: individual or item, in uses associated with 個
senses.period: Warring States use reported; exact transcription and date unverified
senses.text: A reported Warring States slip uses 介 where 個 is intended. The proposed explanation is that the sign 介 was reused to write the separate word 個 because the words may have sounded alike. The cited Mandarin readings jiè and gè, and Baxter–Sagart forms *kˤr[e]p-s and *kˤa[r]-s, do not establish that historical sound match.

senses.gloss: shell or scale; armor; assist; forerunner or intermediary
senses.text: These glosses occur in the supplied material, but no dated sequence links them to one another or to “between.”

senses.gloss: between; mediate or concern oneself with
senses.text: Modern dictionary data include “between,” “mediate,” and “concern oneself with.” They do not establish when these senses arose or how they developed.

limitations.text: The earliest supported textual meaning here is “between”; the graph’s original meaning may have differed, and proposed original senses remain disputed.
The supplied evidence does not establish a chronology connecting “between” with shell or scale, armor, assistance, or intermediary senses.
The reported use of 介 for 個 may be whole-character borrowing, but its direction, date, and historical sound relation are unresolved.

components.text: Early forms show a human figure corresponding to 人; whether it was a separate original part is uncertain.

items.caption: A person-like figure flanked by two marks, matching descriptions of early forms of 介. The marks’ identity and the graph’s original construction remain disputed.
items.alt: Black drawing of a tall central human-like figure with two smaller marks on either side.
items.selection_reason: The visible form illustrates the reported person-and-flanking-marks description of early 介, while the unresolved interpretation cautions against treating its shape as proof of an original meaning.
